title: Another Episode Assessment of the Atrocities Committed on the Sikhs

blocks.text: Dohra:

This did Rattan Singhtell Captain David Murray, That he must ascertain the truth about the Singhs' existence. Did Ahmed Shah arrive prior to the Sikhs' existence (as per Muslim version), Was the Sikh Panth born after the advent of Ahmed Shah Abdali1 ? (1)
lines: This did Rattan Singhtell Captain David Murray,
That he must ascertain the truth about the Singhs' existence.
Did Ahmed Shah arrive prior to the Sikhs' existence (as per Muslim version),
Was the Sikh Panth born after the advent of Ahmed Shah Abdali1 ?

blocks.text: Was the Mughal emperor's version about the Sikh evolution correct, Had the events happened that way or did they happen differently? Was it not a fact that Guru Arjun had been drowned in a river, Had the Mughals not beheaded Guru Tegh Bahadur? (2)
lines: Was the Mughal emperor's version about the Sikh evolution correct,
Had the events happened that way or did they happen differently?
Was it not a fact that Guru Arjun had been drowned in a river,
Had the Mughals not beheaded Guru Tegh Bahadur?

blocks.text: Had the Mughals not slaughtered Tenth Guru's four sons, Had they not killed the innocent infants in their early childhood? Had the Mughals not attacked the Singhs at Muktsar, Had the Sikhs occupied any of the Mughal territories? (3)
lines: Had the Mughals not slaughtered Tenth Guru's four sons,
Had they not killed the innocent infants in their early childhood?
Had the Mughals not attacked the Singhs at Muktsar,
Had the Sikhs occupied any of the Mughal territories?

blocks.text: Innumerable such atrocities had been committed on the Sikhs, Countless is the number of Mughal atrocities to keep their count. Thereafter had the revered Guru sent Banda Singh Bahadur, Who had burnt Wazir Khan's body (the Nawab of Sirhind). (4)
lines: Innumerable such atrocities had been committed on the Sikhs,
Countless is the number of Mughal atrocities to keep their count.
Thereafter had the revered Guru sent Banda Singh Bahadur,
Who had burnt Wazir Khan's body (the Nawab of Sirhind).

blocks.text: Dohra:

Had the Mughals not killed (so many) Singhs, Had they not crushed the Singhs between wheels fitted with nails? Had they not dragged the Singhs' bodies over the uneven ground, Had they not thrown the dead bodies here, there and everywhere? (5)
lines: Had the Mughals not killed (so many) Singhs,
Had they not crushed the Singhs between wheels fitted with nails?
Had they not dragged the Singhs' bodies over the uneven ground,
Had they not thrown the dead bodies here, there and everywhere?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Had the Mughals not crushed the Singhs' heads with batons, Had the Mughals not demolished the Sikh Gurdwaras? Had Bhai Mani Singh's body not been dismembered, Had Bhai Taru Singh's scalp not been peeled off his skull? (6)
lines: Had the Mughals not crushed the Singhs' heads with batons,
Had the Mughals not demolished the Sikh Gurdwaras?
Had Bhai Mani Singh's body not been dismembered,
Had Bhai Taru Singh's scalp not been peeled off his skull?

blocks.text: Countless such atrocities had been committed by the Mughals, Like of which had never been committed by them earlier. Because of these atrocities had Nemesis caught up with them, Thereafter had the Afghans from Kandhar2 ruined Delhi. (7)
lines: Countless such atrocities had been committed by the Mughals,
Like of which had never been committed by them earlier.
Because of these atrocities had Nemesis caught up with them,
Thereafter had the Afghans from Kandhar2 ruined Delhi.

blocks.text: That the Khalsa evolved only after the invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmed Shah, Such a Mughal version about Sikhs' evolution was (absolutely) wrong.
That the Khalsa Panth existed at the time of Aurangzeb, A fact which the Mughals now wished to conceal. (8)
lines: That the Khalsa Panth existed at the time of Aurangzeb,
A fact which the Mughals now wished to conceal.

blocks.text: As bright as the sun had the Khalsa Panth visibly existed, How could clouds of (manipulation) conceal its existence.? The Sun (the Khalsa) which removes darkness from its roots, Who had the guts to eclipse the sun (the Khalsa). (9)
lines: As bright as the sun had the Khalsa Panth visibly existed,
How could clouds of (manipulation) conceal its existence.?
The Sun (the Khalsa) which removes darkness from its roots,
Who had the guts to eclipse the sun (the Khalsa).

blocks.text: Dohra:

Five provinces3 had been taken away from the Delhi rulers, Had Nadir Shah Durrani annexed those five provinces. The same five provinces which had been occupied by Ahmed Shah, Had those provinces been vacated by the Khalsa Panth. (10)
lines: Five provinces3 had been taken away from the Delhi rulers,
Had Nadir Shah Durrani annexed those five provinces.
The same five provinces which had been occupied by Ahmed Shah,
Had those provinces been vacated by the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Sikhs had a legitimate claim over the whole territory, As the Sikhs' claim was based on the sacrifices of their Gurus. Whichever Sikh would be worthy of the revered Guru's grace, He alone would occupy the coveted sovereign's throne. (11)
lines: The Sikhs had a legitimate claim over the whole territory,
As the Sikhs' claim was based on the sacrifices of their Gurus.
Whichever Sikh would be worthy of the revered Guru's grace,
He alone would occupy the coveted sovereign's throne.

blocks.text: Hearing these words did Captain David Murray smile, Perfectly legitimate was the Sikhs' claim indeed, he said. Whatsoever be the divine will of the Divine creator, So shall He cause it to prevail as it pleasath Him. (12)
lines: Hearing these words did Captain David Murray smile,
Perfectly legitimate was the Sikhs' claim indeed, he said.
Whatsoever be the divine will of the Divine creator,
So shall He cause it to prevail as it pleasath Him.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Once again did Captain David Murray remark, Truly had the narrator narrated the whole account. Falsely had the Delhi's Mughal ruler narrated indeed, With malice and factional onesidedness was it tainted. (13)
lines: Once again did Captain David Murray remark,
Truly had the narrator narrated the whole account.
Falsely had the Delhi's Mughal ruler narrated indeed,
With malice and factional onesidedness was it tainted.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thank God, he had not sent it (Mughal version) in writing (to the king), False and incorrect it would have been regarded at London. Thoroughly had he analysed and assessed the whole issue, From the other people also had he counter-checked the facts. (14)
lines: Thank God, he had not sent it (Mughal version) in writing (to the king),
False and incorrect it would have been regarded at London.
Thoroughly had he analysed and assessed the whole issue,
From the other people also had he counter-checked the facts.

blocks.text: Both the Muslim and the Hindu elderly veterans had he consulted, Thoroughly had he enquired the truth from them. The way the narrator had narrated the sequence of events, The same sequence had been corroborated by the learned elders. (15)
lines: Both the Muslim and the Hindu elderly veterans had he consulted,
Thoroughly had he enquired the truth from them.
The way the narrator had narrated the sequence of events,
The same sequence had been corroborated by the learned elders.

blocks.text: Praise be to the Sikh Gurus and praise be to the narrator's wisdom, Perfectly true version had he given of the historical events. True indeed was narrator's version about the formidable Khalsa Panth, Truely had they committed many atrocities on the Sikh Gurus. (16)
lines: Praise be to the Sikh Gurus and praise be to the narrator's wisdom,
Perfectly true version had he given of the historical events.
True indeed was narrator's version about the formidable Khalsa Panth,
Truely had they committed many atrocities on the Sikh Gurus.

blocks.text: The (innocent) Sahibzadas had they killed at both the places, No harm had these innocents Sahibzadas caused. Thereafter, had they laid a seige around the Guru, The Guru's proxy4 had they beheaded in a similar manner. (17)
lines: The (innocent) Sahibzadas had they killed at both the places,
No harm had these innocents Sahibzadas caused.
Thereafter, had they laid a seige around the Guru,
The Guru's proxy4 had they beheaded in a similar manner.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Neither had Guru Gobind Singh killed Aurangzeb's mother, Nor had the Guru killed Mughal emperor's father. Himself had Aurangzeb beseached the Guru to leave for the wild, Himself had he despatched an army to slaughter the Guru. (18)
lines: Neither had Guru Gobind Singh killed Aurangzeb's mother,
Nor had the Guru killed Mughal emperor's father.
Himself had Aurangzeb beseached the Guru to leave for the wild,
Himself had he despatched an army to slaughter the Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
On every count had the Mughals been proved wrong, In both the worlds had they been discredited. One who gets discredited in the Divine Court, His words lose credibility everywhere in the world. (19)
lines: On every count had the Mughals been proved wrong,
In both the worlds had they been discredited.
One who gets discredited in the Divine Court,
His words lose credibility everywhere in the world.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, did Captain David Murray tell the narrator, Fully did he believe in the narrator's version. The same version would he definitely despatch, To the British Sovereign, the king of England. (20)
lines: Thereafter, did Captain David Murray tell the narrator,
Fully did he believe in the narrator's version.
The same version would he definitely despatch,
To the British Sovereign, the king of England.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

From London would this version reach other countries, Wherever the British Christians were in power. Highly glorious was Khalsa Panth's record indeed, Which had been recorded after a thorough investigation. (21)
lines: From London would this version reach other countries,
Wherever the British Christians were in power.
Highly glorious was Khalsa Panth's record indeed,
Which had been recorded after a thorough investigation.

blocks.text: Throughout Syria, Thailand, and China would it reach, Across all the Mohammadan Kingdoms would it spread. Through out Russian and the African countries would it reach, Across many islands and mountain kingdoms would it spread. (22)
lines: Throughout Syria,
Thailand, and China would it reach,
Across all the Mohammadan Kingdoms would it spread.
Through out Russian and the African countries would it reach,
Across many islands and mountain kingdoms would it spread.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Whatever could Rattan Singh manage to narrate, So had he narrated to the best of his ability. Whatever further would he manage to narrate, Listen to that account, dear devout readers. (23)
lines: Whatever could Rattan Singh manage to narrate,
So had he narrated to the best of his ability.
Whatever further would he manage to narrate,
Listen to that account, dear devout readers.
